title: I Used the Catering Service-Charge Math Through Three Banquets

parts.text: I worked banquet one at 6:00 p.m. with a 22 percent service charge the client thought was our tip. Our paystubs said $3 extra. I was twenty-five, server, holding both papers. The captain said service charge is not gratuity, legally, which he only admits in the alley. I photographed the banquet event order, the stub, and the client's signed 22. Then I asked payroll for the mapping. At 9:40 payroll said they would look after the week, which had two more banquets.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Two more 22 percents are coming before payroll looks.

social.video_title: Client signed 22 percent; my stub signed $3 — Part 1/3
social.description: Alley truth, BEO photo, a week of banquets. Would you have waited for payroll's week?

parts.text: Banquet two, I had the clients initial a line I wrote on the BEO copy: service charge is not a tip; add gratuity if you intend one. Half did. My stub still lagged. The captain told me to stop writing on BEOs. I stopped, and emailed the scan to payroll and the hotel AGM instead. Banquet three's client asked me out loud whether the 22 reached us. I said not as of last stub. The room heard. The AGM appeared with a smile that was a meeting.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The room heard the 22 question and the AGM smile is a meeting.

social.video_title: I wrote the not-a-tip line; banquet three asked it aloud — Part 2/3
social.description: Initials, email, a public question. Would you have lied to keep the room warm?

parts.text: Payroll mapped 18 of the 22 to a pool going forward and put a footnote on invoices. Back pay for the three nights posted in two cycles. The captain still likes the alley. I like footnotes. Clients who mean tips can still add one. Math survived three banquets. I serve. I photograph. $3 is not 22 percent of a room. The mapping is a PDF now, which is a kind of raiser. I keep both papers in my locker like a second handbook.

social.video_title: The invoice footnote finally told the truth — Part 3/3
social.description: Pool mapped, back pay, alley still there. Was 22 ever a stub?
